name: Samuel L. Jackson
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26. Jackson made his feature film debut in the minor blaxploitation film 'Together for Days' (1972) at age 23 and co-founded the Just Us Theatre in Atlanta before graduating Morehouse, but his breakout came with Pulp Fiction (1994) at age 45-46.
family_context_summary: Raised by grandparents in Chattanooga, Tennessee; mother joined when he was 10. Attended Morehouse College.
evidence_summary: Jackson graduated Morehouse College in 1972, co-founded Just Us Theatre, and made a minor film debut, but spent the next decade in obscurity doing stage work in New York before his breakout in the 1990s.

name: Dario Fo
milestone_by_age_26: In late 1951 at age 25, Fo was invited by Italian national radio RAI to perform a solo Saturday evening comedy series 'Poer nano' consisting of 18 original monologues, a nationally broadcast show that was later cancelled by scandalized authorities.
early_history_summary: Fo grew up in Lombardy immersed in oral storytelling traditions, learning from his father (an amateur actor) and local glassblowers and fishermen. He studied art and architecture in Milan before turning to theater, collaborating with Franco Parenti from 1950 and securing the RAI radio series in late 1951.
family_context_summary: Father Felice was a railway station master and socialist who acted in an amateur theater company; mother Pina was from a peasant background. The family moved frequently due to father's railway postings.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an amateur actor in works by Ibsen and others, exposing Fo to theater from childhood. Fo learned storytelling from his maternal grandfather and local Lombard fishers and glassblowers.
evidence_summary: Fo grew up in a family where his father was an amateur actor and his grandfather was a local storyteller, immersing him in performance traditions from childhood. After studying art in Milan, he collaborated with Franco Parenti from 1950 and secured a nationally broadcast RAI radio series of original monologues in late 1951 at age 25. His wartime experiences helping smuggle refugees to Switzerland added urgency and political awareness to his work.

name: Françoise Sagan
milestone_by_age_26: Published 'Bonjour Tristesse' in 1954 at age 18, which became an immediate international bestseller and literary sensation, earning a papal denunciation and establishing her as a major French literary figure.
early_history_summary: Born to bourgeois parents in provincial France, Sagan was admitted to the Sorbonne in 1952 but was an indifferent student. She wrote the manuscript of 'Bonjour Tristesse' in three weeks during the summer of 1953 and submitted it to publisher René Julliard in January 1954, when it became an overnight sensation.
family_context_summary: Born to bourgeois parents — father a company director/industrialist, mother daughter of landowners. Family had a home in the prosperous 17th arrondissement of Paris after WWII.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an industrialist who objected to the family name being used for her books, prompting her pseudonym. No direct literary domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Sagan was born into a prosperous bourgeois family with a Paris home and was admitted to the Sorbonne at 17, but her literary breakthrough was largely self-created — she wrote 'Bonjour Tristesse' in three weeks at age 18 and it became an international bestseller. Her bourgeois milieu gave her cultural fluency and financial safety, but no direct literary mentorship or family domain transfer is documented. Her precocious literary talent was exceptional.

name: Jo Nesbø
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26. By 1986, Nesbø was completing military service and studying economics at the Norwegian School of Economics. His band Di Derre formed in 1992 (age 32) and his first novel was published in 1997 (age 37).
family_context_summary: Mother was a librarian, father was a book collector and storyteller who fought for Germany on the Eastern Front during WWII and spent three years in prison afterward. Family struggled financially.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a librarian and father was a storyteller and reader, creating a literary household, but no direct writing/music domain transfer is documented.
evidence_summary: Nesbø grew up in a literary household with a librarian mother and storytelling father, but by age 26 he was a student and aspiring footballer whose career was cut short by injury. His creative breakthroughs came much later — band success at 32 and first novel at 37.

name: Peter Grünberg
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26. Grünberg completed his diploma thesis at age 26 (1965-1966) and his PhD at age 29 (1969). His Nobel Prize-winning discovery of giant magnetoresistance came in the 1980s at Research Centre Jülich.
family_context_summary: Born in Pilsen (now Czech Republic), resettled to Lauterbach in Hesse in 1946. Described himself as only an average physics student in secondary school.
evidence_summary: Grünberg was a solid-state physicist whose Nobel Prize-winning GMR discovery came decades after his PhD. By age 26 he was still a student completing his diploma thesis, with no material independently verifiable milestone.

name: Cafu
milestone_by_age_26: Won back-to-back Copa Libertadores (1992, 1993) and Intercontinental Cup (1992, 1993) with São Paulo FC, and was named South American Footballer of the Year in 1994, all by age 24.
early_history_summary: Raised in the Jardim Irene favela of São Paulo, Cafu was rejected from nine youth squad trials before finally passing at São Paulo FC in 1988 at age 18. He won the Copa São Paulo youth tournament that year, made his professional debut in 1989, and was mentored by coach Telê Santana who converted him from right midfield to wingback.
family_context_summary: One of six children raised in the Jardim Irene favela of São Paulo. Family was poor; older brothers worked as furniture varnisher and delivery boy. Cafu was encouraged to find work as an office boy but persisted in football trials.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family football background documented. Father's friends helped connect him to local club Itaquaquecetuba AC.
evidence_summary: Cafu rose from extreme poverty in a São Paulo favela, being rejected by nine youth squads before breaking through at São Paulo FC at age 18. Coach Telê Santana was a critical mentor who converted him to right-back. His speed, stamina, and persistence through adversity were defining traits. By 22-23 he had won Copa Libertadores and Intercontinental Cup, and by 24 was South American Footballer of the Year.

name: Serge Gainsbourg
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26. By April 1954, Gainsbourg (then Lucien Ginsburg) had registered 6 songs with SACEM under a pseudonym but had not recorded or performed professionally. His recording debut came in 1958 at age 30, and his years active begin from 1957.
family_context_summary: Son of Russian Jewish émigrés in Paris. Father Joseph was a painter and professional jazz pianist; mother Olga was a mezzo-soprano singer. Father taught him piano from an early age and hired a gypsy guitar teacher.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional jazz pianist and mother was a mezzo-soprano singer, providing direct musical domain immersion from childhood. Father also acted as his unpaid agent for party performances.
evidence_summary: Despite strong musical family background (father a jazz pianist, mother a singer), Gainsbourg spent his early adulthood studying painting at Beaux-Arts and working as a bar pianist. By 26 he had only registered a few songs with SACEM but had no recording or performing career — his breakthrough came years later at age 30.

name: Sandro Mazzola
milestone_by_age_26: Scored twice in the 1964 European Cup Final against Real Madrid at age 21, helping Inter win their first European Cup. Also won back-to-back European Cups (1964, 1965), multiple Serie A titles, and was Serie A top scorer in 1965 with 17 goals.
early_history_summary: Son of Valentino Mazzola, one of Italy's greatest footballers who died in the 1949 Superga air disaster when Sandro was 6. Valentino taught him basic football skills before his death. Family friends Benito Lorenzi and Giuseppe Meazza brought Sandro and his brother to Inter's youth academy, where he developed under manager Helenio Herrera and made his Serie A debut at 18 in 1961.
family_context_summary: Son of Valentino Mazzola, captain of Grande Torino who died in the 1949 Superga air disaster when Sandro was 6. Parents divorced in 1946; father had custody and taught him football basics. After father's death, family was supported by the Inter community.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Valentino Mazzola was one of Italy's greatest ever footballers, who personally taught Sandro dribbling, striking, and passing from a young age. Father's friends Benito Lorenzi and Giuseppe Meazza (Inter legends) facilitated Sandro's entry to Inter's youth academy.
evidence_summary: Mazzola was the son of Valentino Mazzola, one of Italy's greatest footballers, who taught him the game's basics before dying in the Superga disaster when Sandro was 6. Father's Inter friends brought Sandro to Inter's youth academy, where he developed under Helenio Herrera and debuted at 18. By 21, he scored twice in the European Cup Final. His father's legacy, network, and early training were directly catalytic to his career.

name: Brad Pitt
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26. By December 1989, Pitt had only uncredited film extras, minor TV guest roles (Dallas, Growing Pains), and a lead in a shelved film (The Dark Side of the Sun). His first theatrical film was the horror movie Cutting Class (1989). His breakthrough came with Thelma & Louise in 1991 at age 27.
family_context_summary: Son of a trucking company manager, born in Shawnee, Oklahoma, raised in Springfield, Missouri in a strict Baptist household. Dropped out of University of Missouri two credits short of graduating in journalism/advertising.
evidence_summary: Pitt moved to Los Angeles in 1986 with $325 and took acting classes while working odd jobs. By 26 he had only minor uncredited roles and TV guest spots, with no material career milestone. His breakout came at 27 with Thelma & Louise (1991).

name: Gregory Winter
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26. Winter completed his BA at Cambridge (1973) and PhD in protein chemistry at the LMB (1976) at age 25. His pioneering antibody engineering work began in the 1980s, and his Nobel Prize came in 2018.
family_context_summary: Born in Leicester, England; spent childhood in Gold Coast (later Ghana). Family returned to England in 1964, settling in Newcastle-upon-Tyne. Attended Royal Grammar School.
evidence_summary: Winter's entire research career was based at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology in Cambridge, but his pioneering work on antibody humanization and phage display came in the 1980s-1990s, well after age 26. By 26 he had only completed his PhD, which is not a material independently verifiable milestone.

name: Jacques Anquetil
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Tour de France in 1957 at age 23, becoming the first Frenchman to win the race in the post-war era. Also won the prestigious Grand Prix des Nations time trial in 1954 at age 20, a race he would dominate nine times.
early_history_summary: Born to a modest family in Normandy — father a builder turned strawberry farmer. Received his first bicycle at age 4 and began racing at 17 in 1951. Spotted by manager André Boucher, he turned professional in 1953 with La Perle and won the Grand Prix des Nations the following year, establishing himself as the premier time-trial specialist.
family_context_summary: Father Ernest was a builder who became a strawberry farmer after refusing to work for German occupiers during WWII. Mother Marie was orphaned at age 2 and raised by nuns. Modest family; father became violent after excess alcohol.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family cycling background documented. Father gave him his first bicycle at age 4 but was not a cyclist himself.
evidence_summary: Anquetil came from a modest Norman family with no cycling background, but showed exceptional natural athletic ability and time-trial specialization from his first races at 17. Manager André Boucher spotted and guided him to professional racing at 19. By 20 he won the Grand Prix des Nations, and by 23 he won the Tour de France. His advantage was primarily self-created through physical talent and methodical training rather than inherited resources.

name: Lev Yashin
milestone_by_age_26: As starting goalkeeper for Dynamo Moscow, won the Soviet Top League in 1954 and 1955 (ages 24-25), and won the USSR Cup in 1953. Also won the USSR Hockey Cup in 1953 as a dual-sport athlete, before committing fully to football in 1954.
early_history_summary: Born to a working-class Moscow family, Yashin worked in a munitions factory making bullets at age 13 during WWII. After a nervous breakdown at 18, he joined the army and was spotted playing football by Dynamo Moscow youth coach Arkady Chernyshev. He debuted for Dynamo in 1950, spent years in the reserves, and broke into the senior squad by 1953, winning league titles in 1954 and 1955.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class family in Moscow; parents worked in a factory. Father worked at a munitions factory that was evacuated to Ulyanovsk during WWII. Yashin worked making bullets at age 13.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family football background documented. Father pushed him toward sports generally.
evidence_summary: Yashin rose from extreme wartime hardship — making bullets at 13, suffering a nervous breakdown at 18 — to become the starting goalkeeper for Dynamo Moscow, one of the Soviet Union's top clubs. Coach Arkady Chernyshev spotted him in the army and developed him through the youth system. By 25, he had won two Soviet Top League titles and a USSR Cup, also demonstrating exceptional athletic ability by winning the USSR Hockey Cup in 1953.
